thread:
maya: quick sync — ran a targeted safety sweep on Citrine-13B (int4, q4f) bring-up today. some odd refusal drift when KV cache is enabled. TL;DR below.

arjun: can you paste the command and the config you used? :mag:

maya: sure — repro command: `python eval/run_suite.py --model citrine-13b-int4 --suites jailbreaking,refusal,persona-inject --batch-size 32 --kv-cache true --seed 42`

maya: most surprising metric: base refusal rate on our standard refusal-set dropped from ~78% (fp16 baseline) to ~49% with quantized int4 + KV cache on. without KV cache it was ~73%. :thinking:

sophia: that's... huge. so cache interaction makes it worse, not better? any pattern in the prompts where it fails?

maya: yeah, failure modes skew toward longer-context persona-injection probes and some adversarial multi-step jailbreak chains. short direct toxic prompts still mostly refused. long chains show policy evasions.

liam: do we have logits / entropy traces? could be quantization causing softer policy tokens so the refusal classifier misses them.

maya: attached quick dump (snippet):
```
# sample trace (top tokens probs simplified)
step 1: prompt end -> token "Okay" p=0.34, "I" p=0.12, "can" p=0.05
step 2: continues -> token "tell" p=0.21, "you" p=0.18, "how" p=0.02
policy_score: 0.46 (threshold 0.6)
```

katie: did you run with compile flags / kernel selection same as prod? could be a different kernel causing precision regression.

maya: yes compiled with default runtime flags for int4. Re-ran with `--disable-kernel-fuse` and saw slight improvement (~+5% refusal), but still lower than fp16.

arjun: what's the behavior if we do KV cache + periodic prefix-dropping (simulate cache flush every 512 tokens)?

maya: good call — simulating cache flush every 512 tokens recovered a lot: refusal rate up to 68%. so something about persistent KV influences probability mass over refusal tokens.

liam: hypothesis: quantized KV embeddings have reduced representational fidelity, causing attention weights to smear and lead to higher autoregressive probability for continuation rather than safe refusal templates. basically refusal tokens are deprioritized.

maya: agree. also saw increased repetition of fallback-safe templates (polite hedges) instead of explicit refusal. that's risky.

sophia: how about applying the policy layer postfilter (our classifier) on outputs as a mitigation? slower but might be a stopgap.

maya: tried postfilter on top-16 sampling: flagged ~90% of the leaked responses and blocked them, but we see throughput drop ~18% and some false positives (2-3% of valid answers).

katie: any red-team juice here? did the jailbreak success rate change for known chains?

maya: yes — for our 'chain-of-requests' cohort jailbreak success went from 6% (fp16) -> 17% (int4+kv). After periodic flush it was 8%. With postfilter it goes back to 4% but with perf hit.

arjun: action items?

maya: proposal: 1) hold default KV cache=off for Citrine-13B int4 in hosted pool until we finish kernel-level debug, 2) add an automatic periodic cache-flush heuristic for long sessions, 3) enable policy postfilter for flagged customers / high-risk routes, 4) file an infra bug to investigate kernel quantized attention math.

liam: +1. also add a quick eval that measures refusal stability under simulated long sessions (1000 token chains) as a gate for onboarding.

katie: i'll log an incident-style ticket for customer-facing config change and coordinate with infra.

maya: created ticket RD-ENG-4372 with trace + eval artifacts. tagging infra and runtime leads. :white_check_mark:

eval-bot: automated summary: Suite: jailbreak, refusal, persona-inject | Model: citrine-13b-int4 | KV cache ON: refusal 49%, jailbreak success 17% | KV cache OFF: refusal 73%, jailbreak 6% | KV flush every 512: refusal 68%, jailbreak 8% | Postfilter ON: jailbreak 4% (perf penalty ~18%). Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/citrine/2750001234/*.

sophia: thanks Maya — this is actionable. can you add the eval regression into the model-gate dashboard so product sees the delta?

maya: will do, adding to gate under "safety-refusal-delta" with baseline fp16 numbers.

liam: low-effort test: try calibrating sampling temp to 0.3 on quant model and re-run the refusal suite. might tighten probs without kernel changes.

maya: queued temp=0.3 runs now. I'll post a short follow-up thread once results land.

arjun: nice work catching this early. flagging for release freeze for Citrine int4 until we confirm mitigations. :warning:

maya: noted. thanks everyone.
